name: Block Store and credential restore
plain: Google Play services can hold a small token that follows a person to a new phone or a reinstall.
meaning: Lets an app restore sign-in without a password. The data is end to end encrypted when a screen lock is set and can survive a reinstall; iOS has no direct equivalent apart from iCloud Keychain.

android.prompt_ui: Restore prompt on new device setup
android.persistence: Stored by Play services; survives reinstall when end to end backup is on
android.revocation: Clear via Play services or device wipe
android.api_surface: Google Play services Block Store API (BlockstoreClient)
android.note: Small byte arrays only; limit about 16 entries of about 4 KB each (unverified)

ios.note: Closest iOS analogs are iCloud Keychain and Keychain persistence

limits.headline: Can keep a small sign in token that follows you to a new Android phone
limits.user_action: You set up a new phone or reinstall the app and approve the restore
can: Store a few small items through Google Play services
Restore them when you set up a new phone
Let you stay signed in after a reinstall
cannot: Store large files; only small pieces of data fit
Work on iPhone, which has no Block Store
Restore without your device setup prompt
limits.reach_label: A small token that follows you
limits.differs: Block Store is Android only. On iPhone the closest tools are iCloud Keychain and Keychain persistence.

story.what_it_is: A tiny token Google keeps that follows you to a new phone so an app can sign you in.

marketing.name: Block Store
marketing.pitch: Google pitches Block Store as a way to restore sign in on a new device without extra steps.

story.for_you: You move to a new phone and the app is already signed in. You did nothing. It feels like magic, and it needs a screen lock.
story.for_makers: Makers keep users signed in across a phone change and avoid the cost of a new login. It can also keep an identity alive across reinstalls.

use_cases.example: A bank app restores your device link so you only confirm with a fingerprint.
A game keeps your account on a new phone with no login.
A streaming app signs you in after you restore.
A store app keeps you signed in after switching phones.
A team sees one person move devices without losing the thread.
A marketer keeps a stable ID across reinstalls.
A fraud tool links an old device to the new one to spot account takeover.

story.android_note: Holds small byte arrays. Restore happens during new phone setup.
story.ios_note: iOS has no direct match. iCloud Keychain and the keychain come closest.

technical_bounds: Needs end to end encryption for cross device
